nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the canopy drives growth in the rainforest, though little of it reaches the dim forest floor.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: Annual rainfall in the Wet Tropics ranges from about 1,200 mm to over 8,000 mm, keeping the forest wet and green.

nodes.name: Soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Fallen leaves, fruit and dead animals are broken down and return nutrients to the forest soil.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and litter invertebrates break down dead plants and animals and recycle nutrients.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Rainforest figs fruit heavily and feed fruit bats, birds and ground feeders.

nodes.name: Satinash and lilly pilly
nodes.desc: Rainforest trees whose fruit and flowers feed cassowaries and spectacled flying foxes.

nodes.name: Fan palm
nodes.desc: A large rainforest palm of the Wet Tropics. Cassowaries eat fruit from the palm family.

nodes.name: Umbrella tree
nodes.desc: Its fruit is eaten by birds, spectacled flying foxes, musky rat-kangaroos and red-legged pademelons. Its leaves feed tree-kangaroos.

nodes.name: Pink-flowered doughwood
nodes.desc: The favoured food plant of the Ulysses butterfly caterpillar.

nodes.name: Southern cassowary
nodes.desc: Forages on the forest floor for fallen fruit and seeds, including some that are toxic to other animals, and passes the seeds on in its droppings.

nodes.name: Spectacled flying fox
nodes.desc: Feeds mainly on rainforest fruit and on flowers of Syzygium and eucalypts. Endangered, partly after a 2018-19 heatwave.

nodes.name: Bennett's tree-kangaroo
nodes.desc: Eats leaves of dozens of rainforest plants, especially umbrella tree, in a small range north of Cooktown.

nodes.name: Musky rat-kangaroo
nodes.desc: Eats fruit, fungi and invertebrates on the forest floor and scatter-hoards fruit, which can help seeds establish.

nodes.name: Ulysses butterfly
nodes.desc: Caterpillars eat leaves of doughwood and similar trees, and adults feed on its blossoms.

nodes.name: Red-legged pademelon
nodes.desc: A small rainforest wallaby that eats umbrella tree fruit.

nodes.name: Australian brushturkey
nodes.desc: Builds a large nest mound of rotting leaf litter. Its eggs are a favourite food of goannas, snakes and dingoes.

nodes.name: Green tree ant
nodes.desc: A weaver ant that builds leaf nests in rainforest trees.

nodes.name: Lace monitor
nodes.desc: Mainly eats carrion but also takes eggs, birds and small mammals, and often raids brushturkey nest mounds.

nodes.name: Cane toad
nodes.desc: An introduced toad that eats ants and many other small animals.

nodes.name: Common tree snake
nodes.desc: Feeds on frogs, skinks and other small reptiles.

nodes.name: Laughing kookaburra
nodes.desc: Takes snakes, lizards, frogs and insects, swooping from a perch.

nodes.name: Scrub python
nodes.desc: A large ambush predator of the rainforest that takes flying foxes, wallabies and tree-kangaroos.
